goal: A condenser microphone set mounted on a desk boom arm, with a shock mount and a foam windscreen.

steps.instruction: Screw the bottom of the boom arm into the hole on top of the desk clamp and tighten it.
steps.why: The desk clamp has a vertical mounting hole and a locking knob, and the arm ends in a threaded post of matching size, so this is where the arm fixes to the desk.

steps.instruction: Slide the plastic adapter onto the front end of the arm and screw it tight.
steps.why: The front of the arm has a short threaded tip and the plastic part has a round sleeve that fits over it; it adapts the arm to the shock mount.

steps.instruction: Screw the base of the shock mount onto the top of the plastic adapter.
steps.why: The shock mount base has a threaded socket and a side knob that lock onto the adapter, giving an angle-adjustable support.

steps.instruction: Insert the microphone from above into the center ring of the shock mount and clamp it.
steps.why: The center ring of the shock mount has elastic bands and the same diameter as the microphone body; it holds the mic suspended to stop vibration.

steps.instruction: Pull the foam windscreen over the mesh grille at the top of the microphone.
steps.why: The black foam cover is slightly larger than the grille so it fits snugly to block plosives; the photo shows the two side by side.
